name: V916 Aql
description: A Cepheid in the Milky Way that pulsates every 13.44 days; its mean radius is 90.7 solar radii.

radius.source: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, V916 Aql: Baade-Wesselink mean radius (solar radii) 90.7 +/- 4.9 (Monte-Carlo)

temperature.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, VizieR J/A+A/635/A33/table1, recno 308, Name='V916 Aql', columns Teff, e_Teff (K): Teff 5500 +/- 250 K from a fit to the spectral energy distribution at mean light (not spectroscopic)

distance.source: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, V916 Aql: Baade-Wesselink distance (pc) 3591.9 +/- 204.6 (Monte-Carlo)

color.reason: Interstellar dust reddens every spectrum of this star, E(B-V) = 1.089 +/- 0.064 (Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10), and its light changes through each pulsation

text.card: A Cepheid in the Milky Way that swells and shrinks every 13.4 days.
text.introduction: Its mean radius, 90.7 solar radii, comes from comparing how fast its surface moves with how its size changes, 3,592 parsecs away.
text.locator: table10, V916 Aql: Per, Rad, Dist

notes: The star pulsates; it is drawn at its mean radius.
No dynamical mass is measured for this Cepheid; its mass is left unmeasured.

gravityRange.source: Luck (2018), AJ 156, 171, table 3 (the spectroscopic gravities of its Cepheid spectra)
